newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka releases Cuban-crewed ship.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka releases Cuban-crewed ship.

text.p: A Cuban-crewed freighter, seized by Sri Lankan authorities off the eastern coast last weekend, was released and will soon sail to Colombo for repairs, a navy spokesman said on Wednesday.
The spokesman said the navy released the 1,674-tonne Caribbean Queen on Tuesday, two days after the Cypriot-flagged ship was seized on suspicion of smuggling arms for Tamil separatist rebels.
Navy patrol boats had taken the freighter to the eastern port of Trincomalee.
The Caribbean Queen was seized after she ignored repeated radio calls and warning shots from military aircraft and started manoeuvres to escape, the Defence Ministry said.
Sri Lankan helicopters fired on the ship when she tried to escape, but none of the 28 Cuban crew were hurt. A search turned up no weapons on board, the navy said.

Cuba's Communist Party newspaper said on Tuesday that Havana was investigating the incident after the ship's captain, Miguel Amaral Ravelo, said his vessel was attacked by two Sri Lankan helicopters in international waters 27.5 miles (44 km) from the Sri Lankan coast.
Sri Lanka's Defence Ministry said the vessel was in Sri Lanka's territorial waters about 10 km (six miles) off the east coast, where Tamil Tiger rebels have jungle bases.
"The Cuban report about the ship's position is wrong," the navy spokesman said. "Furthermore, the vessel was not on the usual international shipping route."
The Cuban daily Granma said the Cuban ambassador in Sri Lanka had visited Trincomalee to talk to the crew.
The ambassador was not available for comment.
Recently, Sri Lanka's navy and air force have stepped up coastal patrols around the island to intercept ships ferrying arms to the Tamil separatists, the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).

The ship's seizure came after the government launched its biggest offensive this year against the Tigers, who are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the Indian Ocean island.

A Defence Ministry spokesman on Wednesday said troops were still consolidating their positions after a 22 kilometre (14 mile) thrust into rebel-held territory northwest of Vavuniya, a government stronghold 220 km (138 miles) north of Colombo.
Officials of the LTTE headquarters in Paris said their international spokesman, Lawrence Thilakar, was not immediately available for comment.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year, but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
